summary.intent: Determine whether a failing Web E2E test (TC08 in recycle-bin.spec.ts) was a real regression or flaky, and if real, fix the root cause introduced by PR #488.
summary.outcome: Root cause was identified and fixed: a two-store desync between Zustand useFolderStore and the SDK client's internal folderTree caused a stale IPNS sequence on delete, producing a 409 that the new merge logic resolved by resurrecting the deleted file. Fix adds reconcileFolderState to the SDK client and calls it in ensureFolderRegistered. Commit was pushed unsigned and a PR + web-e2e dispatch were queued at end of session.

repo: Folder state is maintained in two separate stores: Zustand useFolderStore (web) and the SDK client's internal folderTree. They can desync when sdk-core is called directly, bypassing the SDK client.
File replace (updateFile) publishes folder metadata directly via sdk-core and updates only the Zustand store — the SDK folderTree is never notified, leaving it at a stale IPNS sequence.

Soft-delete is not optimistic: the file only disappears from the UI after deleteToBin() completes an IPNS publish and emits folder:updated. A thrown error is silently swallowed at useFileBrowserActions.ts:515-516.

merge.ts edit-beats-delete branch (lines 47-52) resurrects a locally-deleted child if remote.modifiedAt > base.modifiedAt — correct logic given valid inputs, but produces resurrection when the base snapshot is stale.

folder/index.ts:253-260 has a 409 fallback to union merge when baseChildren is not provided, which can also resurrect deleted items, but delete callers do pass baseChildren so this was not the active branch.

ensureFolderRegistered (sdk-provider.ts:99) no-ops unconditionally when a folder is already registered, treating SDK state as authoritative even after direct sdk-core publishes advance the web store past it.
ci-e2e.yml triggers web-e2e.yml via workflow_call; web-e2e.yml supports workflow_dispatch with a ref input (inputs.ref || github.sha), enabling CI runs against feature branches.
dist/ is gitignored and rebuilt in CI — only source files need to be committed.
integration.test.ts has pre-existing ECONNREFUSED failures requiring a live API server; these appear in broad test runs but are not regressions.

code.finding: edit-beats-delete branch: resurrects a locally-deleted child when remote.modifiedAt > base.modifiedAt. Correct given valid inputs; becomes a bug when base is stale (pre-replace snapshot).

409 fallback: when baseChildren is not provided, falls back to a union merge that never deletes ('deletes may resurrect' warning). Delete callers do pass baseChildren so this branch was not active in TC08.
Delete errors are caught, logger.error'd, and silently swallowed — no user-visible feedback, and the list item is never removed since folder:updated never fires.
After a file replace, the folder-metadata republish (step 6b) is fire-and-forget (not awaited). It bumps modifiedAt and IPNS sequence in the Zustand store only; the SDK folderTree is never updated.

ensureFolderRegistered no-ops when the folder is already registered — SDK internal state is treated as authoritative. This is the desync point: a direct sdk-core publish advances the web store but not the SDK folderTree.
Existing registerFolder test — used as the convention anchor for the new reconcileFolderState unit tests added by this fix.

workflow: Playwright traces capture browser console messages and network call status codes but not request bodies — useful for confirming 409s and resurrection but not for inspecting IPNS sequence numbers.
Browser console.warn messages (e.g. from in-browser merge logic) don't appear in CI server-side job logs — grepping CI logs for browser warnings is a dead end.

Non-contiguous CI failure pattern (fail → pass → fail across commits) is a strong signal toward flakiness, but a single deterministic symptom (same test, same failure mode, 179/180 each time) overrides that heuristic.

1Password SSH signing requires the desktop app to be unlocked and its SSH agent active; background/headless sessions cannot trigger the signing prompt, requiring either user intervention or an unsigned fallback commit.
GitHub artifact downloads can fail transiently and benefit from a retry-with-backoff approach.

friction: 1Password SSH signer was locked throughout the session, blocking signed commits and requiring two failed retries before the user authorized an unsigned commit.
gh CLI job log fetching required multiple retry attempts before succeeding (16k line log).
Browser console output is not captured in CI server-side logs, making it impossible to confirm in-browser merge warnings from the log alone — required downloading the Playwright trace artifact.
Playwright trace request bodies are not captured, so IPNS sequence numbers could not be directly verified from the trace.
Artifact download needed explicit retry-with-backoff tooling to succeed.
The broad SDK test run returned misleading ECONNREFUSED failures that initially appeared to be new failures caused by the fix.
open_items: The unsigned commit will show as 'Unverified' on GitHub and may need re-signing (git commit --amend -S) from the user's machine before the PR can merge if branch protection requires signed commits.
Web E2E run against the fix branch was dispatched but results were not yet available at end of session — TC08 pass/fail is still unconfirmed end-to-end.

Silent delete failure UX (useFileBrowserActions.ts:515-516): a failed delete shows no user-visible error and the file stays in the list with no feedback. Noted as a correctness/UX gap independent of the flake.
The PR creation step was still in progress (branch pushed, PR body written) but the gh pr create command had not yet executed at end of session.
